summary: Preserved candidate PR 2889's unified JIT cache implementation and corrected its remaining DeepGEMM import-order defect by resolving DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR in configurer.py before its supported-platform package probe. Replaced the source-text-only regression with an executable clean-process import-hook test and moved the candidate test into the current registered-test taxonomy.

tests.command: candidate 0d598f3188d250d251ffde2782d53e247c493aa9: clean-process configurer.py load with simulated CUDA SM90 and a synthetic deep_gemm import hook
tests.what_was_measured: The first deep_gemm import observed DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR as <unset>, reproducing review PR 2978's counterexample.
Nine cache contract tests passed, including an executable supported-platform configurer probe that observes the resolved DeepGEMM cache before first import.
All applicable formatting, lint, syntax, policy, and registered-test taxonomy hooks passed.
No whitespace errors in the consolidated correction.

gpu_execution_evidence: The prepared stack is Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. DeepGEMM's affected supported paths are CUDA/MUSA, so no new DeepGEMM GPU execution was claimed. Candidate PR 2889's preserved reports include its independent real ROCm Inductor/Triton compilation evidence.
remaining_limitations: DeepGEMM cache file creation on an actual NVIDIA or MUSA device remains unverified because the prepared host is ROCm.
CUDA driver and FlashInfer CUDA cache writes were not re-executed in this correction; no source change for those paths was justified by the reviewed counterexample.
No native source was changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
